senses.definition: A sending or mission (to do or accomplish something).
An official charge or authority to do something, often used of military officers.
examples: David received his commission after graduating from West Point.

senses.definition: The thing to be done as agent for another.
examples: I have three commissions for the city.

senses.definition: A body or group of people, officially tasked with carrying out a particular function.
examples: The company's sexual harassment commission made sure that every employee completed the on-line course.

quotes.text: A commission was at once appointed to examine into the matter.

senses.definition: A fee charged by an agent or broker for carrying out a transaction.
examples: The real-estate broker charged a four percent commission for their knowledge on bidding for commercial properties; for their intellectual perspective on making a formal offer and the strategy to obtain a mutually satisfying deal with the seller in favour of the buyer.

quotes.text: [T]he scandal was the pretty common one of a corrupt agreement between hotel proprietors and a salesman who took and gave secret commissions, so that his business had a monopoly of all the drink sold in the place.
quotes.reference: 1935, G. K. Chesterton, The Scandal of Father Brown:

senses.definition: The act of committing (e.g. a crime or error).
examples: the commission, preparation or instigation of an act of terrorism

quotes.text: Every commission of sin introduces into the soul a certain degree of hardness.

senses.definition: (transitive) To send or officially charge someone or some group to do something.
examples: James Bond was commissioned with recovering the secret documents.

quotes.text: Stanning, who was commissioned from Sandhurst in 2008 and has served in Afghanistan, is not the first solider^([sic – meaning soldier]) to bail out the organisers at these Games but will be among the most celebrated.

senses.definition: (transitive) To place an order for (often a piece of art).
examples: He commissioned a replica of the Mona Lisa for his living room, but the painter gave up after six months.

senses.definition: (transitive) To put (a ship or boat, etc.) into active service.
examples: The aircraft carrier was commissioned in 1944, during WWII.

quotes.text: The 1.7 mile-long conveyor system was commissioned in November 2022, and will remove one million lorry movements from the roads around West London.

examples: As from our beds, we doe oft cast our eyes, / Cleane linnen yeelds a shirt before we rise, / Which is a garment shifting in condition; / And in the canting tongue is a commission.
